newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-PRICE WINS PLAY-OFF TO MAKE IT TWO IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PRICE WINS PLAY-OFF TO MAKE IT TWO IN A ROW.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Nick Price beat South Africa's David Frost at the first extra hole of a play-off to win the South African PGA Championship on Sunday.
Both men completed the joint South African-European Tour tournament on 269 -- 19 under par -- but Frost bogeyed the replayed 18th, allowing Price to take the title with a par four.
Price also won last week in Sun City and becomes the first man ever to win one million rand ($223,000) in one South African season.
Price was five shots behind Frost at the start of the day and his outward nine of 32, four under par, was in marked contrast to Frost's three over 39.
But Frost got his game back together after the turn and joined Price on 19-under after making back-to-back birdies at 15 and 16.
But a wrong club selection on the short 17th saw Frost's ball plunge into the water bordering the green and a bogey four left him needing a birdie on the last to tie with Price.

He duly obliged with a 14-foot birdie putt but that was the end of his good fortune. The 37-year-old South African hit a bad tee shot on the first play-off hole, the 18th, and a bad second left him short of the green with Price safely on.

Frost could manage only a five to allow Price the luxury of a tap-in par for the title in one of the two major South African tournaments. The other South African major is the South African Open, which Price has never won.
Price said: "I'm exhausted after three weeks in contention. I'm going to fly home to Florida and rest for a week.
South Africa's Nico van Rensburg finished alone in third place at 18 under after shooting 68 for a total of 270.
Two shots further back was another South African, Retief Goosen, who struggled with his putter all day and could manage only a one-under 71.

This was the third and final co-sanctioned event between the South African and European tours. The European tour now moves on to Dubai for the Desert Classic, while the South African tour comes to an end next week in the neighbouring Kingdom of Swaziland. ($ = 4.481 South African Rand)
